Blouberg Vultures

By: Stenette Grosskopf | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
It's a provincial conservation success story... in the heart of the Limpopo Province

Unique Selling Point:
The largest breeding colony of Cape Vultures call Blouberg home... mot people only get to see the birds and their nest sites from afar, but this year, for Vulture Awareness Day, a group of adventurers are taking on the 3-hour hike up the mountain to get closer to these endangered birds.

Summary:
Blouberg Nature Reserve -- described by reserve manager, Johan van Wyk -- is a magical place, like a secret that has not been discovered yet. He's been permanently stationed at the park since 1996 and is the driving force behind this 9300ha conservation success. Through land claims, an onslaught of poaching, prospecting for coal and LEDET budget cuts, he has not given up, and with the help of Friend of Blouberg, this little reserve is thriving. Unlike most other provincial reserves, Johan and the Friends make sure that fences are maintained, tourist facilities upgraded... they do their best to keep the poachers out and the vultures safe.

Further information:
I propose a fun story where we take Mac camping with us at one of the remote camping sites, and then one day will be spent hiking up the mountain. We discover, first-hand what makes this little reserve so special, get close to the vultures and meet some of the people who are passionate about safeguarding this "secret".

Every year (for over a decade), Blouberg hosts an Vulture Weekend, in aid of raising awareness of the plight of vultures. The day is celebrated with a treasure hunt and various fun activities... and this year, a select group of spirited nature-lovers will hike up the mountain to get a closer view of the 900-odd Cape vulture breeding pairs that nest on the cliffs.

But Blouberg is not just about conservation... it's an area with a rich history. The San were the first inhabitants of the area, some 26000 years ago... and it's also the site of an epic battle between the Boers and the Bahananwa people in 1894. Chief Malaboho was eventually overthrown and taken prisoner by Paul Kruger.

Extra Budget Items:
Travel to Blouberg Nature Reserve -- it's about 1000kms there and back
Presenter additional days -- We will need a day to get there and a day back -- so 4 days in total
Accommodation R160pppn (Camping)

Press Release:


Voyage to the Vultures
It’s a vulnerable species, but in Limpopo’s Blouberg Nature Reserve, the Cape Vulture has found a home. High in the mountains, some 1400 breeding pairs nest on the cliffs, and catching a glimpse means a difficult hike up challenging terrain. But that doesn’t dissuade some avid nature lovers from embarking on the sweltering trek. Carte Blanche dons a pair of khaki shorts and hardy boots to join the faithful in their pilgrimage to see the venerable vulture in its natural environment.
Producer: Stenette Grosskopf | Presenter: Govan Whittles

Script:


BLOUBERG VULTURES
V/O
Imagine my excitement!
I'm booked for a story in Blouberg...
Loading the boot Driving


V/O
Daydreaming out the window
An entire weekend of sun, sand and waves… I can’t wait…
Spots signs


V/O
But surprisingly we’re heading North!


V/O
Turns out “Blouberg” is actually a mountain in the lowveld of northern Limpopo, and I need to trade my lilo and flippers for a tent and hiking boots!
UOSOUND
Dankie Meneer!
Vat so!


UPSOUND
Arrive at the gate Blouberg
Blouberg Nature Reserve… Not the Blouberg I thought about, but maybe it’s the Blouberg I need.
V/O
Our visit comes ahead of International Vulture Awareness Day, … And tomorrow we’re hiking up the mountain with a group of nature… and adventure lovers.
UPSOUND
There’s a warthog! Ha! Vlakvark – Good old Blouberg.
V/O
Blouberg is a provincial reserve, and besides a wide variety of wildlife, the main drawcard is the largest breeding colony of Cape Vultures in the world.


UPSOUND
Modumele Wilderness Campsite. That’s us, and oh! Look at our welcoming party! It’s me, Govan, from Carte Blanche… Please don’t walk away, Sir.
V/O
Tonight, I’m camping with camerawoman, Alti and a group of friends at the foot of the mountain.
UPSOUND
Alti: This is my brother-in-law who’s climbing the mountain – he’s had 2 hip replacements and broke both his shoulders.

Govan: Hey Piet, Howzit…
V/O
After more than 5 hours on the road, it feels good to finally put my feet in the sand.
UPSOUND
Irinka: Nice to meet you too…
V/O
But the day is not over yet… Checking in is a bit more labour-intensive than just signing a register… and being shown to your room…
V/O
And after swapping my beach look for something more… hardy…we get on with the all-too-familiar camping rituals…


Light fire UPS
Govan braai


One thing that’s better about a nature reserve compared to the beach… no sand in your meat!
UPSOUND
I really hope I braaied this properly!... laugh


PAUSE
V/O
Vultures are nature’s “clean-up crews”. They help prevent the spread of diseases and parasites. But their numbers are dwindling fast and seven of the 11 species found in Africa are at risk of extinction. Southern Africa’s very own Cape Vulture is listed as vulnerable, with only about six significant breeding sites remaining. And Blouberg is the stronghold for the species.
V/O
But, while this story is about vultures, it’s also about the people who came to see them….
V/O
It’s 6am and some of us are more awake than others!
UPSOUND
Ai, Piet. Hy’t nie koffie gedrink nie.

Ai, Piet. He didn’t drink coffee.
V/O
Our group of campers has swelled to about 30 Blouberg enthusiasts.
Johan
Ons mik vir daai, daai lae gedeelte. Dis waar ons wil oorgaan, okay. Min of meer, ongeveer…

We’re aiming for that, that lower part. The neck. Yes, that’s where we want to cross over.



V/O
Johan van Wyk is the man in charge, not just as reserve manager, but also as our guide for the day…
UPSOUND
Moenie kyk vir die kamera nie… Don’t look at the camera!
V/O
Govan: So, wat gaan ons eintlik doen vandag?

So what are we actually going to do today?

Johan: Ons gaan klim tot daar bo. En dit gaan ‘n uitdaging wees, gaan so bietjie effort vat, maar ons gaan daar uitkom en dan gaan ons daar bo sit en dan gaan ons vir die aasvoëls kyk.

We’re going to climb to the top. It’s going to be a challenge and will take a bit of effort, but we will get there.
V/O
The vultures nest high up in the cliffs, and to get up there is a rather steep 3 and a half km hike… and no actual trail! …
LINK
I was fortunate enough to grow up in a township on the banks of the Buffalo river in the Eastern Cape so bosloop is nie vreemd vir my nie. Maar ek het vergeet hoe baie moet ‘n mens afkyk om seker te maak jy trap nie verkeerd nie and you end up missing the views because of that. Feels good to be back in the bush, though….
V/O
Blouberg was proclaimed in the 1980’s, and today it is the crown jewel of Limpopo’s provincial reserves, largely thanks to Johan’s dedication.
UPSOUND
Govan: Where are you from, Johan?

Johan: Benoni, East Rand.

Govan: Really?

Johan: I grew up there, ja.

Govan: You’re from the East Rand?

Johan: Ja.

Govan: What are you doing all the way out here?

Johan: It is my home here.

V/O
With a passion for conservation he first arrived in the early 90’s.
Johan
Daardie tyd was aasvoëls… nooit gedink dat dit ‘n ou se specialiteit sal raak op ‘n stadium nie. Dis ‘n ding wat jou geskies het, my gekies het.

Govan: So hoe voel jy nou oor die plek, na 30 jaar?

Johan: Man,’n ou leer hom nou baie goed ken, en so… en as dinge verkeerd gaan dan voel ‘n ou redelik opgewerk daaroor. En ‘n ou probeer maar altyd dat dit bly soos wat dit was. ‘N Ou sien maar die veranderinge oor tyd, wat intree; aansoeke van myne wat in die omgewing wil inkom en sulke goeters wat ‘n ou bietjie ontstel. Jy sien hoe verander die landskap. Meer mense, grondpaaie wat wat nou teerpaaie is. Meer influx, meer boerdery uitbreiding…
V/o
But despite these changes, the vultures are still here, successfully breeding – year after year…
UPSOUND
Govan: Is jy alright?

Piet: Ja
V/o
The steep climb is a huge challenge for Piet.

After a double hip replacement, he ended up in hospital earlier this year… with one dislocated, and one broken shoulder… for him, being here is a test of his resilience… as it is for the vultures… and those who look after them…
UPSOUND
There’s just no way to escape gradient, yeh?

Dis taai, hoor!
V/O
Although most of the climbers are regular Blouberg visitors, this is a first for many.
UPSOUND
Ek is nou al 11 jaar wat ons hier bly en ek was nog nooit hier bo nie. En toe die geleentheid nou opkom toe was my naam eerste op die lys, en dis amazing…
Irinka
Ek voel so bietjie haastiger as wat my bene my toelaat om te wees. So, ek het nou besluit ek gaan dit bietjie rustiger vat.
V/O
With a group this size, wildlife sightings are very unlikely, but the veld is full of surprises.
UPSOUND
Daai is ‘n mambavel. Hierdie is nie Nopickus Bergicus… jy will nie daai op jou stoep kry nie.
LINK
It’s just a very tough climb. Lots of scratches and bruises, but that’s allright. And is worth it. These views are incredible. It’s dry, but it is beautiful. Takes your breath away…

Piet!

Piet: Ons is amper daar!
V/O
The last climb is brutal… and the pace is slow….
UPSOUND
Een twee drie
V/O
But this… is not a time for giving up…. And our perseverance is rewarded.
UPSOUND
Kyk hoe lekker is ons hier bo-op die berg. En die aasvoëls is net hier.
JOHAN
Dit is maar die sentinel species, jy weet. As hulle begin swaarkry beteken daar’s iets fout met die omgewing…
UPSOUND
Well done! Okay kom ons gaan soek ‘n boom en pass uit…
V/O
For Piet, reaching the top is a special milestone…
UPSOUND PIET
Govan: Did they give you a recovery time on the hip replacements? Did they tell you what you could do by when?

Piet: They say normally it lasts ten years and you must take it easy and look after yourself.

Govan: Are you taking it easy?

Piet: Yes, I think I’m taking it easy.

Govan: Yeah, what do you think this has shown you? This whole trek up the mountain?

Piet: limits are only there for people who set them themselves…

Govan: That’s true.

Piet: What’s your feeling?

Govan: I discovered something completely different here, dude. I used to think hiking is great when you do it well, you know, but what feels great here is helping people.



The sight of hundreds of vultures above us is an experience that the camera can’t fully capture…

In front of us are the cliffs that the Cape vultures call home…


In August, Johan and his team counted about 1400 active nests. By November, most of the chicks would have fledged, travelling far beyond the borders of Blouberg…
JOHAN
Kyk ons beskerm net sy broeiplek, want as hy wegvlieg hiervanaf dan is hy maar blootgestel aan allerhande risiko’s; vergiftiging, kraglyne, versuip in damme… daai tiepe van goed.


While our plan was to walk right to the top of the cliffs, time and energy got the better of us… and as we catch our breath and soak up the views, the vultures continue to circle …

It seems they too.. understand the magic.. of Blouberg!








PROMO 1 21”
Thousands of Cape Vultures nest in cliffs of the Blouberg, but to get a closer look is no walk in the park.

UPSOUND: It's tough.

We join a group of adventurers, who share a love for this little nature reserve in the heart of the Limpopo bushveld.

UPSOUND: Okay, kom ons gaan soek ‘n boom en pass uit!


PROMO 2 21”
UPSOUND: Een, twee, drie… lead the way Johan!

We’re climbing Blouberg in the Limpopo Province to find out more about the majestic Cape Vulture…

UPSOUND: Johan
PROMO 3 21”
It’s the largest breeding colony of Cape Vultures in the world, and I join a group of hikers on an adventure to get a closer look at these majestic birds.

UPSOUND: Govan

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): It's a provincial conservation success story... in the heart of the Limpopo Province
metadata.Unique Selling Point: The largest breeding colony of Cape Vultures call Blouberg home... mot people only get to see the birds and their nest sites from afar, but this year, for Vulture Awareness Day, a group of adventurers are taking on the 3-hour hike up the mountain to get closer to these endangered birds.
metadata.Summary: Blouberg Nature Reserve -- described by reserve manager, Johan van Wyk -- is a magical place, like a secret that has not been discovered yet. He's been permanently stationed at the park since 1996 and is the driving force behind this 9300ha conservation success. Through land claims, an onslaught of poaching, prospecting for coal and LEDET budget cuts, he has not given up, and with the help of Friend of Blouberg, this little reserve is thriving. Unlike most other provincial reserves, Johan and the Friends make sure that fences are maintained, tourist facilities upgraded... they do their best to keep the poachers out and the vultures safe.
metadata.Further information: I propose a fun story where we take Mac camping with us at one of the remote camping sites, and then one day will be spent hiking up the mountain. We discover, first-hand what makes this little reserve so special, get close to the vultures and meet some of the people who are passionate about safeguarding this "secret". Every year (for over a decade), Blouberg hosts an Vulture Weekend, in aid of raising awareness of the plight of vultures. The day is celebrated with a treasure hunt and various fun activities... and this year, a select group of spirited nature-lovers will hike up the mountain to get a closer view of the 900-odd Cape vulture breeding pairs that nest on the cliffs. But Blouberg is not just about conservation... it's an area with a rich history. The San were the first inhabitants of the area, some 26000 years ago... and it's also the site of an epic battle between the Boers and the Bahananwa people in 1894. Chief Malaboho was eventually overthrown and taken prisoner by Paul Kruger.
